comment: JP2 0081: Suter's commentary, p. 49: chapter 10 continued: the equation of the anomaly by the tangent, with a figure; al-Battānī's columns V-VII; al-Khwārizmī's corrected apogee of Saturn (Sublimatio Saturni examinata); Ibn ʿIrāq's treatise on the halving of the equation; Chasles on the fictitious apogee (notes 1-2).

observations: The page number «49» stands at the head of the page, centred, with a rule below it. At the foot, the signature line of the printed sheet: «D. K. D. Vidensk. Selsk. Skr., 7. Række, hist. og filos. Afd. III 1.», the point after «III» printed so faintly that it hardly shows, on the left, and the sheet number «7» on the right; recorded here, not transcribed as a line. L01: the formula, displayed and centred, continues «Durch die Tangens ausgedrückt, findet man einfacher:» at the end of p. 48 (JP2 0080, L31); its three fractions are built up, written {fr:NUMERATOR|DENOMINATOR}, with a full stop after the last. A speck in the left margin before it; not transcribed.

A figure stands at the right of L04-L20, which are set in a narrower measure at its left; it is not reproduced. As on p. 47 (JP2 0079): the large circle of the ecliptic, A at its top, F at its upper right, B at its bottom, and R, Q, T on its upper left; the inner circle of the deferent, G at its top, K at its bottom; the vertical line A B through G, E′, M (marked by a short stroke), E and K; the small circle of the epicycle about H, which stands on the deferent at the left, with the planet P on it. The lines E′ H Q, E H R and E P T run from the points of the vertical line through the epicycle to the ecliptic; the radius H P, and P S perpendicular to H R. The letters are italic: A, B, E, E′, F, G, H, K, M, P, Q, R, S, T.

L01. Checked: S is the foot of the perpendicular from P to the line E H R, so that tg RET = P S : E S, E S = E H + H S, and with P S = r sin ψ and H S = r cos ψ (p. 48, JP2 0080, L23-L26) tg RET = r sin ψ : (E H + r cos ψ), as printed.

L19-L20: «8s 4° 55′», «8s 2° 3′», the s raised; L20 is set close in the narrow measure. Checked: eight signs and 4° 55′ are 244° 55′, the apogee of Saturn of chapter 18 of the text (p. 14, JP2 0046) and of p. 46 (JP2 0078, L26); eight signs and 2° 3′ are 242° 3′; the corrected apogee of Saturn thus varies by 2° 52′. To be compared with the tables of Saturn. L21: «Dies ist nun wohl der Punkt» begins at the left margin, without the indent of a paragraph, continuing the paragraph of L10.

L25: «Abū Naṣr Manṣūr b. ʿAlī b. ʿIrāḳ» spaced, with the macrons, the dots under ṣ and ḳ and the ʿayn raised before «Alī» and «Irāḳ». L26: «(c. 950—1000)», the long dash set close. L27: the quotation «über die Gründe der Halbierung deı Gleichung bei den Astronomen die dem Sindhind folgten» within German quotation marks; «Halbierung» and «Gleichung» in italics, «Sindhind» upright; the r of «der» is printed without its arm, as a dotless ı; see the critical note.

L31-L37: the passage of Chasles (Comptes rendus 23, 1846, p. 849; see p. 43, JP2 0075, N03-N04), in italics, ending with «Ptolemée.»; «Ptolemée» (L37), as printed; the usual spelling is «Ptolémée», and Chasles's article has not been compared here. L35: «précisement»; see the critical note. L28: «Gleichung ?», the question mark in italics after a thin space (13 px).

N02: «p. XXXXVII», as printed, for the page 47 of the preface (XLVII). «orientalischer Völker»: the word space between the two italic words is narrow (10 px). Spaced type, marked {sp:}: «Batt.», «Kh.», «Ibn al-Adamī», «Abū Naṣr Manṣūr b. ʿAlī b. ʿIrāḳ», «Al-Bīrūnī», «Chasles», «Suter», «Albērūnī», «Sachau».
The colons, semicolons and the question mark stand after the thin space of the edition (11-15 px measured).

critical_notes.evidence: «die Gründe der Halbierung der Gleichung»: the article in the genitive; the r is printed without its arm, so that the word reads «deı»
the same sentence of Chasles, quoted again on p. 50 (JP2 0082, L02), has «précisément», the usual French spelling; here the acute accent on the second e is missing
the list of misprints, p. [237] (JP2 0271, L11), reads «p. VII» for «p. I»; the introduction is printed on pp. VII-XXV (contents, p. [III], JP2 0007)
